question.text: Under SEBI IA Regulations, which type of investment adviser must appoint either a compliance officer or an eligible independent professional to monitor compliance?

answer.text: All investment advisers regardless of structure
Only non-individual investment advisers (body corporate, LLP, partnership firm)
Only individual IAs with more than 150 clients
Only IAs registered with BSE Administration & Supervision Ltd

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that a non-individual investment adviser must appoint either a compliance officer or an eligible independent professional to monitor compliance. Individual IAs are not subject to this requirement, since the individual adviser is personally responsible for compliance. The Trap: Candidates may assume that every IA must designate a compliance officer, or that the requirement is to appoint a compliance officer alone. The source-stated rule offers an either/or option (compliance officer OR an eligible independent professional) and is limited to non-individual IAs. Note: Source basis is p.349 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025).
